findings.evidence: `@[expose] def toGrp` appears at lines 46-48 and is used only to define the category instance at line 52; the public morphism accessors start at lines 62 and 94.
findings.fix: Make `toGrp` private or at least remove `@[expose]`; keep consumers on `Hom.toOverHom`, `Hom.toSchemeHom`, and the preservation lemmas instead.
findings.issue: `AbelianVariety.toGrp` is an exposed implementation bridge for the induced category, not a roadmap-facing operation on abelian varieties.

findings.evidence: The only hits for `mk'` are the constructor at lines 56-59; the file has id/comp/toScheme lemmas but no `mk'` projection lemma.
findings.fix: Add `[simp]` lemmas such as `Hom.toOverHom_mk' : Hom.toOverHom (Hom.mk' f one_f mul_f) = f` and the corresponding `toSchemeHom` restatement.
findings.issue: `Hom.mk'` has no characteristic lemma identifying the underlying over/scheme morphism of the constructed homomorphism, so downstream users cannot use the constructor without unfolding the wrapper.

findings.evidence: `Hom.ext_toSchemeHom` is declared without attributes at lines 116-120; Mathlib registers `Grp.hom_ext` with `@[... (attr := ext)]` in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Grp.lean:120`.
findings.fix: Annotate `Hom.ext_toSchemeHom` with `@[ext]`, matching the underlying `Grp.hom_ext` API.
findings.issue: The extensionality lemma is not registered as an ext lemma, so uniqueness/equality proofs for the universal property will not be available through `ext`.

summary: The new hom type has the right shape, but its public API still forces downstream users toward implementation details and leaves the constructor under-characterized.
